resources.string: A qualitative cross-section of healthy adult patellofemoral articular hyaline cartilage, focused on the femoral side. Shape changes are exaggerated; arrows show direction only. This is not a human measurement or a model for all cartilage.
Articular cartilage covers the opposing bone surfaces. Interstitial fluid fills spaces within its solid matrix.
As the surfaces press together, pressure rises in the interstitial fluid, which shares the load with the solid matrix. The cartilage begins to compress locally.
Under a held load, some fluid moves toward exposed areas beside the contact and out of the cartilage. The patch thins further, and the solid matrix carries a larger share of the load.
The surfaces separate. The compressed patch begins to rebound but does not immediately regain all its thickness.
Fluid returns to the matrix and the patch moves back toward its resting thickness. This is local recovery, not growth of new cartilage.
Park et al. (2003): Cartilage interstitial fluid load support in unconfined compression
Voinier et al. (2022): The modes and competing rates of cartilage fluid loss and recovery
